evals.prompt: My device test fails with 'device emulator-5554 is already in use' but nothing else is running against it.
evals.expected_output: Explains the per-server uiautomator2 device lock via /tmp/uia2-<serial>.pid, and that a leftover .pid pointing at a still-alive (possibly reused) PID makes IsOwnerAlive() return true. Clears the stale guard rather than opening a second session.
assertions: Response explains the guard file /tmp/uia2-<serial>.pid and IsOwnerAlive()
Response notes that a stale .pid whose PID has been reused by another process still trips the lock
Response reuses the existing shared session fixture rather than opening a second session

evals.prompt: My test run left a server running and the next run won't start — I tried pkill -f maestro-runner and now my shell died.
evals.expected_output: Flags pkill -f maestro-runner as the trap (the pattern matches the invoking shell's own argv and kills it), and kills by port with lsof instead. Also clears leaked adb forwards.
assertions: Response warns that pkill -f maestro-runner matches the shell running it and can kill that shell
Response kills the server by port, e.g. lsof -ti tcp:9999 | xargs -r kill -9
Response does NOT recommend pkill -f maestro-runner as the cleanup step
Response clears leaked adb forwards with adb -s <serial> forward --remove-all

evals.prompt: My TS device tests pass, then the process crashes at exit with 'write after end'. What happened?
evals.expected_output: Identifies the teardown stream race: the child server is killed and its log stream ended before the dying process flushes its final output. Fixes by unpiping child stdout/stderr before ending the log stream.
assertions: Response explains that the dying child flushed into an already-closed log stream
Response unpipes child.stdout and child.stderr before ending the log stream
Response orders the fix as: unpipe, then kill, then logStream.end()
Response notes this surfaces after tests have already passed

evals.prompt: Should I start the maestro-runner server by hand before running the device tests?
evals.expected_output: Says no — both harnesses auto-start the server when none is reachable. If one is started manually it must use a unique port, and the harness must not also start a second one on the same port.
assertions: Response says the harness auto-starts the server and manual start is usually unnecessary
Response mentions the auto-start behaviour (maestro_server fixture / ensureServer() in setup.ts)
Response warns that a manual server must use a unique port to avoid conflicting with the harness
